packet.headline_seed: Thousands of anti-migrant protesters march in South Africa amid heavy police presence

what: Thousands of anti-migrant protesters march in South Africa amid heavy police presence

clean_source_blocks.text: Co-ordinated protests have taken place across the country with a heavy security presence in most cities Thousands of people have marched in South Africa's main cities to demand that all undocumented migrants leave the country. Police officers - backed by private security guards - have been deployed because of fears that protests could turn violent. Anti-migrant groups had set Tuesday as the deadline for undocumented migrants to leave. Many foreigners have already fled to escape violence and intimidation. South African police say 25,000 have been repatriated so far. Most are from other African countries. One undocumented Malawian told the BBC he was "happy to be going back" but "heartbroken" to be leaving behind four young children. 'They came with machetes' - deadline looms for migrants to leave South Africa
Foreigners have already left South Africa ahead of the deadline set by anti-migrant groups.

Reuters | Posted: June 30, 2026 1:34 PM | Last Updated: Just now Movement's leader says it would hold weekly marches until objectives are met Caption: Anti-immigrant protesters in South Africa march past activists against xenophobia on the day of an unofficial deadline set by anti-immigrant groups for all undocumented migrants to leave, in Cape Town on Tuesday. (Esa Alexander/Reuters) Caption: Foreign nationals sleep in front of a government office in Durban on Tuesday. (Rogan Ward/Reuters) Caption: Anti-immigrant protesters march in Durban on Tuesday, the day of an unofficial deadline set by anti-immigrant groups for all undocumented migrants to leave South Africa. (Rogan Ward/Reuters)

The Ministry of Police said the protests had largely been peaceful across the country, with isolated incidents of looting. However Police Minister Firoz Cachalia confirmed that the army was deployed "on a contingency basis" in "parts of Johannesburg" as well as Durban. Police also confirmed the arrest of three more people in Hillbrow, a suburb in Johannesburg with a high migrant population, after two people were injured during protests. According to police, the trio "opened fire at protesters who were passing through the street" and the marchers retaliated by "torching the suspects' vehicle". Among the injured was a 17-year-old. Some protesters threw bricks, breaking the windows of some homes in Yeoville, another suburb where many African migrants live. Shops in the city centre were closed, while police visibility is high on major streets.

original_article.research:
[Lähde: BBC World]
Co-ordinated protests have taken place across the country with a heavy security presence in most cities

Thousands of people have marched in South Africa's main cities to demand that all undocumented migrants leave the country.

Police officers - backed by private security guards - have been deployed because of fears that protests could turn violent. Anti-migrant groups had set Tuesday as the deadline for undocumented migrants to leave.

Many foreigners have already fled to escape violence and intimidation. South African police say 25,000 have been repatriated so far. Most are from other African countries.

One undocumented Malawian told the BBC he was "happy to be going back" but "heartbroken" to be leaving behind four young children.

'They came with machetes' - deadline looms for migrants to leave South Africa

The Ministry of Police said the protests had largely been peaceful across the country, with isolated incidents of looting.

However Police Minister Firoz Cachalia confirmed that the army was deployed "on a contingency basis" in "parts of Johannesburg" as well as Durban.

Police also confirmed the arrest of three more people in Hillbrow, a suburb in Johannesburg with a high migrant population, after two people were injured during protests.

According to police, the trio "opened fire at protesters who were passing through the street" and the marchers retaliated by "torching the suspects' vehicle". Among the injured was a 17-year-old.

Some protesters threw bricks, breaking the windows of some homes in Yeoville, another suburb where many African migrants live.

Shops in the city centre were closed, while police visibility is high on major streets.

In a neighbourhood in Germiston, about 15km (nine miles) from Johannesburg, demonstrators went to homes, evicting residents they suspected were foreign nationals and handing them over to police officers, insisting they check their documentation, local media report.

Police said they had arrested five people for the alleged looting of a foreign-owned shop in Johannesburg's biggest township, Soweto.

About 10 people were also arrested for looting in KwaZulu-Natal province, while a woman was arrested for assaulting a police officer and a man for "intimidation" following reports of a foreign national being beaten up, police said.

Businesses in central Durban, the main city in the province, were also shut.

payload.title: Tuhannet maahanmuuttovastaiset mielenosoittajat marssivat Etelä-Afrikassa
payload.summary: Etelä-Afrikan suurissa kaupungeissa järjestettiin koordinoituja mielenosoituksia, joissa vaadittiin paperittomien siirtolaisten poistumista maasta. Poliisi ja paikoin armeija varautuivat väkivaltaisuuksiin.
payload.content:
Tuhannet maahanmuuttovastaiset mielenosoittajat ovat marssineet Etelä-Afrikan suurissa kaupungeissa vaatien, että kaikki paperittomat siirtolaiset poistuvat maasta. Turvajärjestelyt olivat laajat, koska viranomaiset pelkäsivät protestien muuttuvan väkivaltaisiksi, ja poliisin mukaan maasta on tähän mennessä palautettu 25 000 ihmistä.

## Mielenosoituksia useissa kaupungeissa

Mielenosoitukset järjestettiin samana päivänä, jonka maahanmuuttovastaiset ryhmät olivat asettaneet epäviralliseksi määräajaksi paperittomien siirtolaisten lähtemiselle. Protesteja nähtiin muun muassa Kapkaupungissa ja Durbanissa, ja niihin osallistui tuhansia ihmisiä. Kapkaupungissa maahanmuuttovastaiset mielenosoittajat marssivat myös muukalaisvihaa vastustavien aktivistien ohi.

Poliiseja oli kaduilla runsaasti, ja heidän tukenaan oli yksityisiä vartijoita. Poliisin näkyvyys oli suuri erityisesti keskeisillä kaduilla, ja osa kaupungin keskustan liikkeistä pysyi suljettuna. Durbanissa ulkomaalaisia nukkui hallintorakennuksen edustalla samana päivänä, jolloin määräaika umpeutui.

Monet ulkomaalaiset ovat jo lähteneet Etelä-Afrikasta väkivallan ja uhkailun pelossa. Suurin osa palautetuista on muista Afrikan maista. Eräs paperiton malawilainen kertoi BBC:lle olevansa helpottunut paluusta, mutta samalla murheissaan, koska joutuu jättämään Etelä-Afrikkaan neljä pientä lastaan.

## Viranomaiset kertovat välikohtauksista

Etelä-Afrikan poliisiministeriön mukaan mielenosoitukset sujuivat eri puolilla maata pääosin rauhallisesti, mutta niihin liittyi yksittäisiä ryöstelytapauksia. Poliisisministeri Firoz Cachalia vahvisti, että armeijaa oli sijoitettu varotoimena osiin Johannesburgia sekä Durbaniin.

Johannesburgin Hillbrow’n kaupunginosassa poliisi pidätti kolme ihmistä sen jälkeen, kun kaksi henkilöä loukkaantui protestien aikana. Poliisin mukaan pidätetyt avasivat tulen kadulla kulkeneita mielenosoittajia kohti, minkä jälkeen marssijat sytyttivät epäiltyjen ajoneuvon tuleen. Loukkaantuneiden joukossa oli 17-vuotias.

Toisessa Johannesburgin kaupunginosassa Yeovillessa osa mielenosoittajista heitti tiiliä ja rikkoi joidenkin asuntojen ikkunoita. Sekä Hillbrow’ssa että Yeovillessa asuu paljon Afrikan maista tulleita siirtolaisia. Maahanmuuttovastaisen liikkeen johtaja on kertonut, että marsseja on tarkoitus jatkaa viikoittain, kunnes liikkeen tavoitteet täyttyvät.

Poliisi kertoo, että 25 000 ihmistä on palautettu maasta tähän mennessä.
Viranomaisten mukaan protestit olivat pääosin rauhallisia, mutta Johannesburgissa raportoitiin väkivaltaisista välikohtauksista.
